chunks: Ahmad, from Al-Husayn, from Fazalat, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who leads the women (in prayer) when there is no man with them, in the obligatory prayer, he said: Yes, and if there is a boy with him, let him stand beside him.
ai.seo_question: Who should stand beside the Imam when a man leads women in prayer with a child present?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of a man leading women in congregational prayer (Salat al-Fard) even in the absence of other adult males, a ruling derived from the principle of maintaining the validity of the prayer structure. It further specifies that if a young boy is present, he should stand beside the Imam rather than in the front row, preserving the hierarchical order of leadership while allowing for familial participation. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the flexibility of prayer arrangements within the household while maintaining the distinct role of the male Imam.

en.hubeali: Ahmad, from Al Husayn, from Fazalat, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Ibrahim Bin Manmoun,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the man who led the women (in Salāt), there not being (another) man with them, in the Obligatory (Salāt)’. Heasws said: ‘And even if there was a male child with him, so let him stand to his side’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn al-Husayn has narrated from Fadalah from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from Ibrahim ibn Maymun who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about a man who leads women in obligatory Salah (prayer) where there are no other men. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so and if there is a child he stands up on his side.’”
